children: The S&P Global Services PMI eased to 57.8 in August 2026 from 58.3 in July and missing analysts' forecasts of 59 but remaining firmly in expansionary territory.
The reading was the second-highest in nearly three and a half years, pointing to continued solid growth.
New business increased for a fourth straight month, supported by strong domestic demand.
New export business also increased modestly, but at a slightly weaker pace than July, as geopolitical uncertainty continued to restrain foreing demand.
Job growth was maintained, but hiring cooled to a four-month low, as some firms chose not to replace leavers.
Firms appear reluctant to expand their workforces as they increasingly look to technology to improve productivity amid rising labour costs.
Business confidence fell to a three-month low and remained below trend, despite expectations of improving geopolitical and macroeconomic conditions over the year ahead.

title: Spain Services Sector Unexpectedly Slows
